title: Engobe layer brushwork on air-dry clay
subtitle: Applying coloured slip-paint layers to an air-dry surface for a matte earthy finish
excerpt: Engobe is a high-clay slip with a more paint-like consistency than ordinary liquid slip. Applied to air-dry clay with a brush in layered washes, it gives a matte earthy surface finish without a kiln. This technique produces a hand-painted look with visible brush marks, layered colours, and a surface that reads closer to ceramic than plain painted clay.
sourceNotes: Engobe brushwork technique derived from traditional slip-decoration practice adapted for air-dry clay surfaces. No-kiln adaptation derived from contemporary craft methodology.

glossaryTerms.definition: A clay-rich slip with a more glaze-like formulation, applied as a decorative coating. On air-dry clay it functions as a matte coloured surface treatment.
Air-dried but unfired clay. The stage at which engobe should be applied.

content.text: An
engobe

is a slip with more flux and filler than plain liquid clay. In a kiln it fires to a matte surface. On air-dry clay it dries and bonds to the surface. The result is a clay-rich matte finish that looks different from acrylic paint. The surface is slightly chalky and gritty. This is the look of unglazed ceramics.

Use commercial pottery slip for this technique. Choose coloured-slip-red, coloured-slip-black, or coloured-slip-white from the master table. Thin the slip until it is easy to brush. Apply it to an air-dry clay surface. No kiln is needed.
What you need
A
bone-dry

air-dry clay piece. Ready-mixed pottery slip or DIY slip (air-dry clay dissolved in water to a thick-cream consistency). A wide mop brush for base coats and a liner brush for detail. Acrylic sealant to protect the finished surface.
Applying the engobe
Ensure the air-dry piece is fully bone-dry before applying any slip. Applying slip to a partially-dry piece will cause the base to absorb moisture unevenly and may cause cracking.

Thin the slip with water to the consistency of single cream. Stir thoroughly: slip settles fast. Apply the first coat with the mop brush, loading the brush well and laying the slip on in single broad strokes. Do not over-brush: too many strokes drag the slip before it sets and leave uneven coverage.

Allow the first coat to dry: 20 to 30 minutes at room temperature. The slip dries lighter than it looks when wet. Apply a second coat in the same direction as the first for even coverage, or in the opposite direction for a visible cross-hatched texture.

For multi-colour layered effects: apply the base colour first and allow to dry fully. Then apply a second, lighter or darker colour, and before it dries completely wipe the raised surfaces of any texture with a dry cloth to allow the base colour to show through the recesses.
Allow all slip coats to dry thoroughly: a minimum of two hours. Apply two coats of acrylic sealant over the dried slip to bind the surface and protect it from moisture.
What it looks like when right

The finished surface should be even in coverage with no bright patches or bare spots. Brush marks can be visible as texture, or smoothed out depending on how the coats are applied. The surface reads chalky and matte: the clay-rich quality of the slip gives a completely different look from acrylic paint, which tends to sit on the surface as a plastic film.
Common mistakes
Applying slip to wet clay: the base absorbs moisture unevenly. Wait until bone-dry.
Slip flaking off after drying: the slip was applied too thick in one coat, or the air-dry clay surface was dusty. Brush off any surface dust before applying.
Surface looks patchy: slip not stirred thoroughly before each coat; brush strokes too heavy in some areas. Stir the slip every few minutes during application.

rows.problem: Slip cracks in a map-like pattern as it dries
rows.cause: Applied too thick in one coat; slip too concentrated
rows.fix: Thin the slip further and apply in thinner, more coats. Let each coat dry fully before the next.

rows.problem: Colour much lighter than expected when dry
rows.cause: Normal: slip lightens significantly when dry on air-dry clay
rows.fix: Build coverage in three or four thin coats. Test a small sample on a dry clay offcut before committing to the full piece.
